messages.subject: Multiple Imputation and Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)?
parts:
Hello! I have been wondering for a while whether there exist some packages or ready-made routines to do multiple imputation for exploratory factor analysis? Particularly when one has ordered categorical data. 

I was checking on semTools but it seems it only has a function for CFA.

Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Imputation and Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)?
parts: packages or ready-made routines to do multiple imputation for exploratory factor analysis? Particularly when one has ordered categorical data. I was checking on semTools but it seems it only has a function for CFA.

Indeed, the runMI() function and efaUnrotate() functions in semTools were not designed to cooperate.  But efaUnrotate() is just a shortcut for specifying EFA models as CFA models (i.e., all indicators load on all common factors, no residual covariances, orthogonal common factors), which is something you can do manually.  If you specify the "EFA" models manually (one each for the number of factors you want to test extracting), then you can fit each to your list of imputed data sets using runMI(). 

Or you can get the model specifications "automatically" from efaUnrotate() by using it on the first imputed data set, once for each number-of-factors you want to extract.  Once you have those fitted models (which are lavaan models), you can extract the parameter table from each one to use as the "model" argument in runMI() instead of model syntax. Here's an example for a 3-factor solution (assuming you use Amelia, which is arbitrary).

impOut <- amelia(myData, m = 20, ords = ...)
impList <- impOut$ imputations
## get model specification for a 3-factor solution
PT3 <- parTable(efaUnrotate(impList[[1]], nf = 3, ordered = ...)
## fit model to imputed data sets
out3 <- cfa.mi(PT3, data = impList, ordered = ...)
